ut.title: Ultrasonic Testing & Thickness Gauging | Birmingham, AL
ut.description: Ultrasonic thickness testing and UT weld inspection for Birmingham foundries, pipe plants, steel fabricators and process piping, run at your site. Get a quote.
ut.h1: Ultrasonic Testing (UT) Inspection in Birmingham, Alabama
ut.html:
Atlantis NDT carries out ultrasonic thickness testing and ultrasonic weld inspection at industrial sites around Birmingham: wall surveys on process piping and pressure vessels, thickness checks on pipe, fittings and cast components, and shear-wave examination of structural and pressure-boundary welds. Technicians travel to your site with calibrated gauges, work to a written procedure and report against the code your owner or engineer names. Send your UT scope for a quote and we reply within one business day.

Where ultrasonic testing is used in Birmingham

Birmingham exists because iron ore, coal and limestone sit close together in Jones Valley, and the city still carries that heritage in its metalworking base. Cast and ductile iron pipe, fittings and valves came out of the district's foundries for more than a century, steel is still made at the Fairfield mill west of downtown, and fabricators in the surrounding counties build structural steel, pressure equipment and conveyor and mining hardware. Each of these produces a different ultrasonic job.

At a foundry or pipe plant the question is usually wall thickness on a finished or semi-finished casting, where a wall that ran thin against the pattern shows up as a low reading before the part ever reaches a trench. At a process plant or utility the question is remaining wall on carbon steel piping and vessels that have been in service for decades. At a steel fabricator the question is whether groove welds on beams, plate girders and pressure parts are sound inside, where a visual check cannot see. The Birmingham region also has chemical, food and beverage, hospital and university buildings with steam and compressed-gas systems, and each one has piping that someone has to gauge on a schedule.

What UT finds and what it misses in iron and steel

Ultrasonic testing sends high-frequency sound into the part and times the echoes. In steel that gives a clean reading of remaining thickness and a view of internal discontinuities in welds: lack of fusion, cracks, slag, and porosity clusters. Corrosion and erosion show as a thinner back wall, and laminations in plate show as a reflector parallel to the surface.

The method has real limits on the material Birmingham is known for. Gray cast iron has coarse graphite flakes that scatter and absorb sound, so thickness work on it needs lower-frequency probes and a technician who accepts a noisier signal; fine structure inside a gray iron casting is generally not something UT resolves. Ductile iron attenuates less and can be gauged with the right probe and a procedure qualified on a sample of the same pipe. Rough, scaled, painted or pitted surfaces degrade coupling, which is why surface preparation belongs in the scope. UT also cannot size a crack tip you cannot scan to, and it will not tell you a flaw is harmful. It gives a location, a size and an amplitude that the code then judges.

Codes and acceptance criteria for Birmingham work

The method itself follows ASME Section V: Article 4 for ultrasonic examination of welds, Article 5 for materials, and Article 23 (SE-797) for contact thickness measurement. Acceptance comes from whichever construction or in-service code governs the item. Process piping examined under ASME B31.3 uses the ultrasonic provisions in paragraph 344.6 and the criteria in Table 341.3.2. Pressure vessels built to ASME Section VIII Division 1 use Mandatory Appendix 12 for weld examination. Structural steel fabricated to AWS D1.1 follows the ultrasonic clauses for groove welds in Clause 8 of the 2020 edition. In-service piping and vessels follow API 570 and API 510, where the owner's authorized inspector sets the inspection plan and Atlantis provides the thickness data and flaw findings.

Alabama regulates boilers and pressure vessels under the Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act, Title 25, Chapter 12 of the Code of Alabama, administered by the Alabama Department of Workforce. The state requires operating certificates and installation permits, and its construction list refers to the ASME Code, the National Board Inspection Code and API 510. OSHA process safety management under 29 CFR 1910.119(j) adds a mechanical integrity expectation at covered plants. We confirm the governing documents with you before any scan.

How a thickness survey is done

A thickness survey starts with a layout. Condition monitoring locations are marked on a drawing or isometric, a grid is laid out on the area of interest, and the surface is cleaned to bright metal or to a smooth coating. The technician calibrates a dual-element probe on a step block of the same material and checks the zero before and during the job. Dual-element probes handle pitted and corroded steel better than single-element probes because the transmit and receive crystals are separated.

Readings are taken with a couplant suited to the surface temperature. On hot lines a high-temperature couplant and probe are used, and readings are corrected for temperature. We favor an A-scan display over a bare digital readout, because the waveform shows when a gauge is locking onto a lamination or doubling the back-wall echo on thin wall. Each point is recorded against its location so a later survey can be compared reading to reading, which is how a corrosion rate is established for piping and vessels.

Shear-wave examination of welds

Weld inspection uses angle-beam probes, typically 45, 60 or 70 degrees, on a wedge that sends a shear wave into the weld and heat-affected zone from both sides where access allows. The technician builds a distance-amplitude curve on a reference block containing side-drilled holes, scans at a defined gain above reference, and evaluates each indication by amplitude, length and position.

In Birmingham this typically means beam-to-column and girder welds on a fabricator's floor, longitudinal and circumferential seams on pressure parts, and repair welds on process piping. Weld profile, root geometry and thickness decide whether a clean scan is possible, and thin-wall pipe welds and small-diameter branch connections are often better served by another method. Where UT cannot be applied cleanly we say so in the proposal instead of forcing it.

Who does the work

Ultrasonic work is performed and interpreted by Level II technicians qualified under Atlantis's written practice, which follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Procedures are written to the code, reviewed and approved by an ASNT NDT Level III, and the technician follows the approved revision on the job. Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, leads that oversight. Atlantis is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001. Atlantis has no office in Birmingham; technicians are mobilized to your site for the agreed scope. If your own program requires a specific qualification scheme or a customer's flow-down requirement, tell us at the quote stage so the personnel and procedure are matched to it.

What the UT report contains

A usable report identifies the component, the line or vessel number and the drawing reference. It names the procedure and revision, the code and acceptance criteria, the instrument, probes, wedges and calibration blocks with their calibration status, and the technician and certification level. For thickness work it gives the nominal wall, the minimum required wall if you supply it, and every reading in a grid or table with locations. For weld work it lists each reportable indication with its position along the weld, depth, length, amplitude and the accept or reject call against the named criteria, with a sketch. Raw data, calibration sheets and photographs of the area are retained so an engineer or authorized inspector can audit the result.

Planning a UT job in Birmingham

Birmingham's summers are hot and humid, and surface temperature on uninsulated piping and tank shells can pass the working limit of ordinary couplant by midday. Planning scans for morning hours, shading the work area or using high-temperature materials keeps readings repeatable. Winter is mild, though cold mornings can matter on exposed structural steel. Plant access in the district generally involves a safety orientation, badging and permits for hot work areas, so give us the site contact early. The interstate junction at Birmingham connects I-20, I-59 and I-65, which makes travel from other cities straightforward for the teams we mobilize, and rail yards, mills and pipe plants along those corridors are routine work sites. Scaffold, rope-free access and insulation removal are normally the owner's responsibility and belong in the scope.

UT, MT or PT for your Birmingham job

Choose ultrasonic testing when you need remaining thickness or the inside of a weld. Choose magnetic particle inspection in Birmingham for surface cracks in carbon steel, such as toe cracks on a crane runway weld or a fatigue crack at a lifting lug. Choose liquid penetrant testing in Birmingham for surface-breaking flaws on stainless steel, aluminum or any non-magnetic part. Many jobs use two: ultrasonic scans find the volumetric flaw, and a surface method confirms whether it reaches the skin. The national overview of ultrasonic testing services describes the method in general, and the Alabama inspection services hub lists the other work we support in the state.

Training your own UT technicians

Plants and fabricators around Birmingham often want their own people able to gauge thickness. Atlantis delivers UT Level 1 training and UT Level 2 training built on SNT-TC-1A, with practice time in the ultrasonic testing simulator. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies, so the program is designed around your written practice. See the NDT training page for Birmingham for how courses are delivered.

faq.q: Can ultrasonic testing measure wall thickness on cast iron pipe in Birmingham?
faq.a: Yes, with limits. Ductile iron can be gauged with an appropriate probe and a calibration block of similar material. Gray cast iron scatters sound, so lower frequencies and a qualified procedure are needed, and readings are less crisp.

faq.q: What do I need to prepare before a UT thickness survey?
faq.a: Provide a drawing or line list, access to the surfaces, removal of insulation or scale at the measurement points, and the nominal and minimum wall if you have them. Clean, bare or smooth-coated metal gives repeatable readings.

faq.q: Does UT replace radiography on welds?
faq.a: Only where the code and the owner permit it. Substitution is agreed in advance with the engineer and the authorized inspector. UT often suits thick sections and planar flaws, while some thin-wall welds fit other methods better.

faq.q: Which codes govern ultrasonic weld inspection for structural steel?
faq.a: Structural steel fabricated to AWS D1.1 follows its ultrasonic clauses for groove welds, and the method itself is run to ASME Section V Article 4 when the contract calls for it. The contract names the controlling document.

faq.q: Can you gauge thickness on hot piping at a Birmingham plant?
faq.a: Often, using high-temperature probes and couplant with temperature correction. Very hot surfaces may need the line to cool or an extended-range setup, which we confirm during scope review.

faq.q: Who decides whether a UT indication is acceptable?
faq.a: The acceptance criteria in the governing code decide. Our Level II technician evaluates the indication against those criteria, an ASNT Level III reviews procedures and reports, and your engineer or authorized inspector makes fitness decisions.

faq.q: Do you have an office in Birmingham?
faq.a: No. Atlantis has no office in Birmingham. Technicians are mobilized to your plant, yard or fabrication shop for the agreed scope, with equipment calibrated before the trip.

faq.q: What does the ultrasonic report include?
faq.a: It lists the component, procedure and revision, code, equipment and calibration, technician and level, every reading or reportable indication with its location, and the accept or reject call. Thickness grids and weld sketches are attached.

faq.q: Can my own staff learn ultrasonic thickness gauging?
faq.a: Yes. Level 1 and Level 2 UT courses prepare technicians to gauge thickness and, at Level 2, to evaluate welds. Your employer completes the practical and certification under its written practice.

mt.title: Magnetic Particle Inspection (MPI) | Birmingham, AL MT
mt.description: On-site magnetic particle inspection (MT) for Birmingham steel fabrication, cranes, castings, pressure parts and structures, using yokes and prods. Request a quote.
mt.h1: Magnetic Particle Inspection (MT) in Birmingham, Alabama
mt.html:
Atlantis NDT runs magnetic particle inspection on carbon and low-alloy steel at fabrication shops, plants, rail and industrial yards in the Birmingham area: weld toes and root passes, castings and forgings, crane and lifting hardware, and structural connections. Technicians travel to your site with yokes, prods, particles and UV equipment, work to a written procedure, and report against the code your engineer names. Request a magnetic particle quote and we reply within one business day.

Where magnetic particle inspection is used in Birmingham

MT is a steel-shop method, and Birmingham is a steel-shop city. The district grew on pig iron and steel, and it still has structural fabricators, pressure vessel and tank shops, foundries and machine shops that handle ferromagnetic material every day. The surface cracks that matter most in that work are toe cracks in fillet and groove welds, fatigue cracks in lifting lugs and trunnions, hot tears and shrinkage cracks in steel castings, and quench cracks in heat-treated parts.

Typical Birmingham jobs include examining welds on beams, columns and built-up girders before shipment, checking crane hooks, runway rails and hoist attachments in mills and warehouses, examining trailer and rail car components, and looking at weld repairs on pressure vessels and piping supports in process plants. Mining and bulk-handling equipment in the surrounding counties, such as conveyor frames, idler supports and bucket hardware, takes a lot of cyclic load and is a regular source of cracks in welded details.

What MT finds and what it misses

Magnetic particle inspection works only on ferromagnetic material: carbon steel, low-alloy steel, martensitic stainless, and iron. A magnetic field is induced in the part, and a surface or slightly subsurface discontinuity leaks flux that holds fine iron particles in a visible line. Austenitic stainless steel, aluminum, copper and most nickel alloys do not support the method, and those parts need liquid penetrant testing in Birmingham instead.

MT is quick and sensitive on tight, shallow cracks that a visual check misses, but depth is limited. Subsurface flaws are found only if they are shallow and the field is strong, and a flaw parallel to the field direction produces little or no indication, which is why two examinations at roughly right angles are required. Heavy paint, scale and weld spatter hide indications, and coatings above a qualified thickness reduce sensitivity. Non-relevant indications from changes in section, sharp radii or magnetic writing are common and have to be interpreted, not just counted.

Codes and acceptance criteria

Method requirements come from ASME Section V Article 7, and ASTM E1444 and E709 cover the practice and the guide. Acceptance is set by the construction code. ASME Section VIII Division 1 puts magnetic particle methods and acceptance in Mandatory Appendix 6. Process piping under ASME B31.3 refers to paragraph 344.3 and the criteria in Table 341.3.2. Structural work to AWS D1.1 follows its visual and magnetic particle clauses, and bridge steel built to AWS D1.5 for state transportation work has its own acceptance tables. If your shop works to a customer specification, we align the procedure to that document.

In Alabama, boilers and pressure vessels fall under the state's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act and the Alabama Department of Workforce. The state's list of construction standards includes the ASME Code and the National Board Inspection Code, so repair and alteration work on registered equipment brings NBIC repair rules into the inspection plan. We confirm which documents govern before the job.

Technique: yokes, prods and particles

For field and shop work the usual tool is the electromagnetic yoke. An AC yoke needs a lifting power of at least 10 pounds at the pole spacing used, and a DC or permanent-magnet yoke at least 40 pounds, checked with a standard weight before use. Prods push current through the part and suit heavy sections and castings, but they can arc-burn the surface, so their use is controlled by procedure and often prohibited on finished or critical parts.

Visible dry or wet particles under white light suit most structural and weld work outdoors. Wet fluorescent particles under UV-A light give higher sensitivity for fatigue-critical parts and are examined in a darkened area with the light intensity checked first. The technician prepares the surface, applies the field in two directions, applies particles during magnetization, observes and records indications, then demagnetizes if residual magnetism could interfere with later welding, machining or service. Field indicators and a pie gauge or equivalent verify field strength and direction.

Who does the work

Technicians who perform and interpret the examination are Level II under the company's written practice, based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. An ASNT Level III approves the MT procedure and reviews reports. Atlantis is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001. Because there is no Atlantis office in Birmingham, crews are mobilized to your site for the agreed scope and work to your safety rules. For fatigue-critical or high-consequence parts the proposal states the particle type, lighting, field strength verification and acceptance basis in plain terms, so your quality manager can approve the approach before work starts.

What the MT report contains

The report names the component and its drawing or tag, the procedure and revision, the governing code and acceptance standard, the technique used (yoke or prods, wet or dry, visible or fluorescent), the equipment with calibration or lift-test status, and the technician and level. It records surface condition, the field directions applied, and every relevant indication with its location, length and orientation, with a sketch or photo. Each indication gets an accept or reject call against the named criteria, and repaired areas are re-examined and documented after the fix. Demagnetization status is recorded where required.

Planning an MT job in Birmingham

Wet particle methods behave differently in the heat and humidity of a Birmingham summer, and surfaces above the temperature limit of the particle carrier cannot be examined until they cool. Fluorescent work needs a dark enclosure or a shaded area, which is harder in open yards at midday, so evening or enclosed setups are common. Rain, dew and condensation spoil dry particle work and wet down electrical contact points. Access, grinding to remove spatter and paint, and the owner's hot work permits should be in the plan. The I-20, I-59 and I-65 corridors make most district sites easy to reach, and plant and mill sites typically require a safety orientation and badging that we arrange with your contact in advance.

MT, PT or UT for your Birmingham job

Use MT for surface cracking in steel when speed and sensitivity matter. Use dye penetrant inspection in Birmingham when the material is non-magnetic or the surface is machined and open. Use ultrasonic testing in Birmingham when the concern is thickness loss or an internal weld flaw. The national page on magnetic particle testing services explains the method in general, and the Alabama hub shows the full list of inspection work we support. The MT versus PT comparison helps when you are deciding between the two surface methods.

Training your own MT technicians

Shops that run frequent inspections often prefer to qualify their own inspectors. Atlantis delivers MT Level 1 training and MT Level 2 training to SNT-TC-1A, with practice questions in the NDT practice tests. Your company certifies its personnel under its written practice. The Birmingham NDT training page covers delivery for sites in the area.

faq.q: Does magnetic particle inspection work on stainless steel?
faq.a: Only on magnetic grades such as martensitic stainless. Austenitic stainless steel, aluminum and most nickel alloys are not magnetic, so liquid penetrant testing is the surface method for those parts.

faq.q: How deep can MT find a flaw?
faq.a: MT is a surface method that also detects very shallow subsurface flaws. It does not locate deep internal flaws, so ultrasonic testing is used when the concern is inside the metal.

faq.q: Why does MT need two field directions?
faq.a: A crack shows best when it crosses the magnetic field. Examining in two directions at roughly right angles makes sure cracks running either way are detected.

faq.q: Do you use prods or yokes on finished parts?
faq.a: Yokes are preferred on finished and critical parts because they do not pass current through the surface. Prods can arc-burn the metal, so their use is limited by procedure and agreed with you first.

faq.q: When is wet fluorescent MT needed instead of dry visible particles?
faq.a: Fluorescent wet particles give higher sensitivity and suit fatigue-critical parts, castings and machined surfaces. Visible dry or wet particles are normal for weld and structural work outdoors.

faq.q: Is demagnetization always required?
faq.a: No. It is required when residual magnetism could interfere with later welding, machining, instruments or service. The procedure and your specification state when it applies, and the report records it.

faq.q: Can MT be done through paint?
faq.a: Thin, tightly bonded coatings may be tolerated if the procedure is qualified for that thickness. Heavy or loose coatings reduce sensitivity and should be removed at examination areas.

faq.q: Do you have an office in Birmingham?
faq.a: No. Atlantis has no office in Birmingham. Technicians are mobilized to your shop or site for the agreed scope and bring calibrated yokes and lighting.

faq.q: Can we train our own staff in magnetic particle testing?
faq.a: Yes. MT Level 1 and Level 2 courses are built on SNT-TC-1A, and your company completes qualification and certification under its own written practice.

pt.title: Liquid Penetrant Testing & Dye Penetrant | Birmingham, AL
pt.description: Liquid penetrant testing and dye penetrant inspection (PT) for Birmingham welds, castings, stainless and aluminum parts, performed at your site. Request a quote.
pt.h1: Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT) in Birmingham, Alabama
pt.html:
Atlantis NDT performs liquid penetrant testing, often called dye penetrant inspection, on welds, castings, machined parts and process equipment around Birmingham. PT finds cracks and other flaws open to the surface in stainless steel, aluminum, nickel alloys, bronze and other non-porous materials, as well as in steel. Technicians travel to your site with penetrant kits, cleaners and developers and report against the code your engineer names. Ask for a penetrant testing quote and we reply within one business day.

Where liquid penetrant testing is used in Birmingham

The Birmingham district made its name on iron, but the work that reaches penetrant inspection today is broader. Valve and fitting makers machine and finish brass, bronze and stainless bodies, and Alabama's foundry history includes bronze valves and pipe fittings at scale. Fabricators weld stainless and aluminum for food, beverage, chemical and hospital piping. Pump and compressor repair shops handle shafts, impellers and casings. Process plants and utilities in the region have austenitic stainless tubing and piping where magnetic methods are of no use.

Penetrant is also the follow-up to other methods. A magnetic particle indication on a weld may be confirmed on the surface with PT, a repair groove is checked before welding starts, and a final weld pass is checked after grinding. Where a part is machined and smooth, PT shows fine fatigue cracks at keyways, threads and fillets that would be easy to smear over.

What PT finds and what it misses

Penetrant testing detects only discontinuities open to the surface: cracks, laps, seams, porosity and lack of fusion that break the skin. The penetrant is drawn into the opening by capillary action, excess is removed, and a developer pulls the trapped liquid back out so it shows as a visible line or spot. It works on any non-porous material, ferrous or not, and needs no electricity or special geometry.

It cannot see a flaw that is closed, buried, or filled with oxide, paint, grease or smeared metal. Peened, shot-blasted, ground or machined surfaces can mask openings by smearing metal across them, so surface preparation and sometimes etching are part of the procedure. Rough or porous surfaces, such as as-cast sand surfaces, create broad background that hides small indications. A negative PT result means no open flaw was shown at the sensitivity the technique provides, not that the part is free of internal defects.

Codes and acceptance criteria

ASME Section V Article 6 sets the method requirements, and ASTM E165 is the general industry practice. Acceptance is taken from the governing code. ASME Section VIII Division 1 uses Mandatory Appendix 8 for penetrant methods and acceptance, ASME B31.3 uses paragraph 344.4 with the criteria in Table 341.3.2, and AWS D1.1, D1.5 and D1.6 apply to structural, bridge and stainless welding work. Aerospace-type specifications often call for ASTM E1417 and a specified sensitivity level, and where a customer provides a specification we write the procedure to it.

Alabama regulates boilers and pressure vessels through the Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act and the Alabama Department of Workforce. Repairs and alterations on registered pressure equipment follow the National Board Inspection Code, which brings penetrant examination into repair documentation. OSHA process safety management in 29 CFR 1910.119(j) also expects documented mechanical integrity inspections at covered process plants.

Technique step by step

PT is a process, and each step affects the result. The technician cleans the area to remove oil, scale, paint and weld spatter, then dries it. Penetrant, red visible dye or fluorescent, is applied and left on the surface for a dwell time stated in the procedure. Excess is removed with the method the procedure specifies, whether a solvent wipe, water wash or post-emulsification step, taking care not to wash penetrant out of the flaw. A thin, even coat of developer follows, and the part is examined after the development time.

Solvent-removable visible penetrant is the standard field choice for welds and large components. Fluorescent penetrant gives higher sensitivity and is examined under UV-A light in a darkened area. Test blocks or comparator panels verify that materials are working, and the batch numbers of penetrants, cleaners and developers are recorded because contamination of the materials is a known source of false results. After examination the part is cleaned, which is important on stainless and nickel alloys where residues can matter in service.

Who does the work

PT is performed and interpreted by Level II technicians qualified under Atlantis's written practice, which follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A. An ASNT Level III approves the procedure and reviews the report. Atlantis is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001. Atlantis has no office in Birmingham; technicians are mobilized to your plant or shop for the scope you approve, with materials sourced in matched, traceable lots. If your quality program restricts halogens or sulfur on stainless steel or nickel alloys, tell us at quote stage and the proposal will specify materials with certified low-contaminant content.

What the PT report contains

The report identifies the component and location, procedure and revision, governing code and acceptance criteria, penetrant type and method, the manufacturer and batch of penetrant, remover and developer, surface temperature, dwell and development times, and the technician and level. Every relevant indication is recorded with location, length and type (linear or rounded), with a photograph or sketch. Each is given an accept or reject call, and areas that were repaired and re-examined are documented separately. Post-cleaning is noted where required.

Planning a PT job in Birmingham

The standard temperature range for the part and the materials in ASME Section V Article 6 is 40 to 125 degrees Fahrenheit, and a procedure qualified outside that window is needed beyond it. Birmingham sun can push a steel surface well above the upper limit in summer, so shading, early starts or cooling are planned in. Cold winter mornings are less severe than in northern cities but can still dip near the lower limit on exposed steel. High humidity lengthens drying times and can dilute water-washable penetrant, so we plan the process around the weather. Plant access, scaffold, ventilation and solvent use in confined spaces should be settled in advance with the owner's safety group.

PT, MT or UT for your Birmingham job

Use PT when the material is non-magnetic, the surface is machined or the flaw must be confirmed as surface-breaking. Use magnetic particle inspection in Birmingham on carbon steel when speed matters. Use ultrasonic inspection in Birmingham for internal flaws and thickness. The penetrant testing overview covers the method nationally, and the guide to ASME Section V Article 6 goes through the standard in detail. For more of our work in the state see the Alabama inspection hub.

Training your own PT technicians

Penetrant testing is among the quickest methods to learn well, and many shops qualify their own staff. Atlantis delivers PT Level 1 training and PT Level 2 training to SNT-TC-1A, with practice in the penetrant testing simulator. Your employer certifies under its written practice, and the NDT training page for Birmingham explains how delivery works.

faq.q: What materials can liquid penetrant testing be used on?
faq.a: Any non-porous material, including carbon and stainless steel, aluminum, nickel alloys, bronze and titanium. It is not suited to porous materials or rough as-cast sand surfaces without special procedures.

faq.q: Can PT find subsurface flaws?
faq.a: No. Penetrant testing detects only flaws open to the surface. Internal flaws need ultrasonic testing, and surface cracks in steel can also be found by magnetic particle inspection.

faq.q: What is the difference between red dye and fluorescent penetrant?
faq.a: Red visible penetrant is examined in normal light and is common for field welds. Fluorescent penetrant is examined under UV-A light in darkness and has higher sensitivity for fine cracks.

faq.q: How hot or cold can a part be for PT?
faq.a: The standard range in ASME Section V Article 6 is 40 to 125 degrees Fahrenheit. Outside that range the procedure must be qualified at the temperature in use.

faq.q: Why does surface preparation matter so much?
faq.a: Oil, paint, scale and smeared metal block flaw openings, and penetrant cannot enter a blocked crack. Cleaning, and sometimes etching after grinding or machining, restores the openings.

faq.q: Do you control contaminants on stainless and nickel alloys?
faq.a: Yes, when your specification requires it. Materials with certified low halogen and sulfur content are selected, batch numbers are recorded and parts are cleaned afterward.

faq.q: Do you have an office in Birmingham?
faq.a: No. Atlantis has no office in Birmingham. Technicians are mobilized to your plant or shop for the agreed scope and bring matched, traceable penetrant materials.

faq.q: What does a PT report show?
faq.a: It lists the component, procedure and revision, code, penetrant type and batch, temperatures and times, technician and level, and each indication with its location, size and accept or reject call.

faq.q: Can our staff learn dye penetrant inspection?
faq.a: Yes. PT Level 1 and Level 2 courses follow SNT-TC-1A and include simulator practice. Your employer certifies personnel under its own written practice.
